title: LogVerdict verdict database
description: Curated rulings on Windows log signatures. Editors that understand JSON Schema will validate and autocomplete against this; Test-LogVerdictDatabase enforces the same rules plus the ones a schema cannot express.

schemaVersion.description: Loading a version this build does not understand is a hard failure, not a best effort. v3 adds per-rule sources[] so attribution obligations travel with the rule. v4 adds the 'reliability' match source, which an earlier build cannot collect at all. v5 adds the correlations[] array.

correlations.description: Curated pairings of rules that mean more together than apart. Deliberately curated and never inferred: on a single machine the loudest signature co-occurs with everything, so a discovered correlation is almost always an artefact of volume rather than a cause.

id.description: Shipped correlations use LVC-nnnn so they cannot collide with rule ids.

sources.description: Where this ruling came from, same shape as a rule's sources[].

correlation.description: Vocabulary follows the Sigma Correlation Rules Specification v2.1.0 so anyone who reads Sigma can read these. The WINDOW does not: Sigma buckets time into fixed intervals, which misses a pair straddling a boundary while matching an unrelated pair at opposite ends of one bucket. This slides instead.

type.description: temporal: every referenced rule occurred inside one window. temporal_ordered: additionally, their first occurrences follow the declared order.

rules.description: Rule ids that must co-occur. For temporal_ordered the array order is the required order.

timespan.description: Sliding window width: 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d. An unparseable value is skipped loudly rather than defaulted, because a correlation that silently never fires looks exactly like a healthy machine.

group-by.description: Sigma's grouping keys. On a single PC the useful ones are service name, process image and device instance - never user or host, which are constant.

id.description: Unique and stable. Shipped rules use LV-nnnn; site-local rules should use their own prefix so they cannot collide.

status.description: Sigma-aligned lifecycle. deprecated and unsupported rules are retained for traceability but never applied to a signature.

verified.description: When this ruling was last checked against reality. Guidance ages; the validator fails rules older than 24 months.

locale.description: Required when messagePattern matches event text, which Windows renders from localized resources. Compared on the language part only, so en-US also matches en-GB.

verdict.description: benign is suppressed by default. Do not reach for critical unless hardware or data integrity is genuinely at risk.

title.description: One line, plain English, no jargon.

plain.description: What actually happened, for someone who does not already know.

why.description: Why it does or does not matter. This is where judgement belongs.

action.description: The concrete next step. 'Ignore.' is a complete and often correct answer.

confidence.description: How certain the ruling is. Restating a self-describing message is high; adding interpretation is medium.

references.description: Sources backing the ruling. Strongly encouraged for anything asserting what a vendor recommends.

falsepositives.description: When this ruling is wrong. The most valuable field in the file: a verdict is only useful if the reader can tell it does not apply to them.

sources.description: Where this ruling came from, and under what terms. Required for anything derived from a licensed corpus: CC-BY-4.0 obliges attribution and an indication of changes, and DRL-1.1 obliges the author be shown at match time.

uri.description: Where the claim can be checked.

licence.description: Terms the source is published under, e.g. CC-BY-4.0, DRL-1.1, MIT. Omit for a source merely consulted rather than derived from.

author.description: Original rule author. DRL-1.1 requires this be displayed on every match.

retrieved.description: ISO date the source was read.

modified.description: True when the prose was adapted rather than reproduced. CC-BY-4.0 requires changes be indicated.

match.description: More match keys means higher specificity, and the most specific matching rule wins.

source.description: Which collector produced the signature. 'reliability' is Reliability Monitor, whose records are structured like events and match on provider and event id.

channel.description: Event channel name, the text-log target name such as CBS or SetupAPI, or 'Reliability'.

provider.description: Event provider. A trailing * matches a provider family.

messagePattern.description: Regex against the sample message. For event sources this is locale-dependent, so declare 'locale' too.

escalate.description: Rate-based escalation, for signatures that are noise at a trickle and a fault at volume.
